current_episode.title: 115: Fell in Love With the Costa del Sol this Summer & Want to Make the Move? [Start here]

guest.bio_context: Warner co-hosts The Costa Property Podcast alongside his partner and relocated from Ireland to the Costa del Sol 10 years ago with two young children. He and his co-host have personal experience buying, flipping, and renovating investment properties on the Costa del Sol, and now run a property and relocation advisory business helping international buyers make the move. He describes himself as the dreamer in the partnership while his co-host handles the planning side of their operation.

context.real_quote: We knew that the life that we had in Ireland wasn't sustainable for the growth of our family and our children and we just made that decision.
key_stats: Spanish banks lend between 60% to 70% of loan-to-value for foreign buyers purchasing on the Costa del Sol
Property purchase costs: budget 10% to 12% on top of the list price (e.g. a 350,000-euro property requires an additional 10%-12% in taxes and fees)
The hosts relocated from Ireland to the Costa del Sol 10 years ago (circa September 2014, referenced as 10 years ago to the exact month at recording)
Costa del Sol averages 325 sunshine days per year, cited as a key lifestyle factor for relocation
WL Costa Properties location quiz takes less than 60 seconds to complete and delivers a personalised location profile by email
One partner should plan for approximately 3 months focusing on family integration before returning to full employment after relocation

pending_qa.q: What employment options exist for people relocating to the Costa del Sol who still need to work?
pending_qa.r: Relocators have several options: approaching their current international employer's HR department about a global mobility program if a legal entity exists in Spain, seeking employment with an international company based in the area, or setting up as self-employed. Employment status is particularly important to clarify in advance for non-EU visa applicants, as employment stipulations form a key part of visa requirements.

pending_qa.q: How should couples or families manage the transition period when both partners need to work after relocating to the Costa del Sol?
pending_qa.r: The hosts advise that one partner should take the lead on employment while the other focuses on integrating the family, particularly settling children into school, for the first three months. They made the mistake of both jumping into employment simultaneously with two small children, which forced one of them to step back, so they recommend having this honest discussion before the move.

pending_qa.q: How do you know if your desire to move to the Costa del Sol is more than just post-holiday blues?
pending_qa.r: The hosts distinguish between normal end-of-holiday sadness and a deeper, persistent feeling that life needs to change. They recommend returning home, letting routine resume, and if the internal noise does not go away, planning another trip to the Costa del Sol and beginning to research seriously rather than dismissing the feeling.
